The sky hung like a man at the gallows above a ruined world - the wastelands flooded with the water of a thousand moons, rubble forming the forlorn sea floor. Mountain peaks dotted the seascape like island chains, packed with refugees - those few who survived.

High above the world, a rift opened up - a rift to a forgotten world, one past mind and reality. Tymoro was long gone - but a hand slipped through, and snapped its fingers.

Gravity lost its hold on Gaea's sun. Pulsing outwards at almost the speed of light, the fuel of nuclear fusion formed a deadly corona of plasma. The star had gone supernova. Inwards it swept, until the halo embraced the planet that had once formed the cradle of life.

All they saw was a flash of light, and then their mortal forms were no more than shadows flash-burned to the stone on which they stood. Oceans boiled away and the atmosphere vaporized, crowning the planet with a wreath of flame. Finally the planet itself carbonized and melted, brushed away by the hand of the god-like maelstrom of the sun's wrath. All was gone, then the supernova subsided, as much as a supernova *could* subside. Left in the center of the wreckage was a bleak orb of pure malice, consuming the various gases left behind by the supernova.

The hand snapped again.

Portals to the Primrose opened up, connecting the black hole to the entirety of time and space in one small area. Other portals snapped into existence all throughout the universe, inside stars and planets, all drawing into the maw of the final gasp of the universe, the grand black hole. The hand receded, and the rift closed.

Stars collapse inwards on themselves and go nova, suffering their planets the same fate as Gaea, only for the dust and rubble to be swept into the singularity. Again and again, solar systems winked out. Galaxies faded into nothing, and nebulæ vanished as if sucked up through a great cosmic straw.

Finally there was nothing. No Primrose, no Gaea.

Only black.

The being which had just destroyed the universe was satisfied. But something felt off, all was not as it should be.

Slowly, something dawned on the being: It was not alone. Something had followed it, chasing it through the rift from the universe it had just destroyed. Something strange, twisted, hateful.

The destroyer of the universe barely had time to scream.
